newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end mixed, T-bonds turn up late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end mixed, T-bonds turn up late.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed narrowly mixed as September T-bonds continued to grind higher in slow light trade ahead of Friday's U.S. Producer Price Index (PPI), traders and analysts said.
Rumblings of mortgage-backed dealer interest, coupled with relief that September T-bonds held losses at 113-16/32 -- above support at 113-12/32 to 113-11/32 -- lifted prices.

One U.S. dealer bought 1,000 September T-bonds, which helped push the contract through the 113-26/32 to 113-28/32 area. Light buy-stop orders were touched off and forced locals to cover short positions.
"Longs are really well-placed ahead of PPI tomorrow," a T-bond trader said, noting that total open interest has been expanding during September bond's rally.
On Wednesday when September T-bonds rose to a fresh seven-month high of 114-03/32, total open interest rose more than 16,000 to over 501,000.
Strength also spilled over from the 10-year Treasury note pit where another U.S. dealer bought about 7,000 September 10-years, traders said.
However, order flow was extremely light in T-bonds, with traders estimating total volume at 270,000 contracts.
They said the fundamental backdrop of low inflation, coupled with concerns about the U.S. Treasury department's supply, would boost September T-bonds to 114-06/32 to 114-09/32 in the near term.
According to a Reuters poll, traders, on average, are looking for PPI to stay unchanged and the core rate to rise 0.1 percent, from down 0.3 percent overall and excluding food and energy in May.
However, several traders expressed caution about the low inflationary environment, noting increases in weekly chain store sales through the July Fourth holiday in the United States.
They said September T-bonds could rise as high as 114-24/32 before staging a correction to the 112-24/32 area.

At the end of pit trade, September T-bonds were off 1/32 at 113-28/32, 10-year T-notes were steady at 109-15/32, December T-bills and Eurodollars were also steady at 94.76 and 94.07, respectively, September five-year notes were flat at 107-00 and munibonds were also unchanged at 119-11/32. ((Chicago Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
